edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De praescriptionibus adversus haereticos, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Regula est autem fidei, ut jam hinc quid defendamus profiteamur, illa scilicet qua creditur, unum omnino Deum esse, nec alium praeter mundi conditorem; qui universa de nihilo produxerit, per Verbum suum primo omnium emissum; id Verbum, Filium ejus appellatum, in nomine Dei varie visum a Patriarchis, in Prophetis semper auditum, postremo delatum ex Spiritu Patris Dei et virtute in virginem Mariam, carnem factum in utero ejus, et ex ea natum egisse Jesum Christum; exinde praedicasse novam legem, et novam promissionem regni coelorum; virtutes fecisse; fixum cruci, tertia die resurrexisse; in coelos ereptum sedisse ad dexteram Patris; misisse vicariam vim Spiritus Sancti, qui credentes agat, venturum cum claritate, ad sumendos sanctos in vitae aeternae et promissorum coelestium fructum, et ad profanos adjudicandos igni perpetuo, facta utriusque partis resuscitatione cum carnis restitutione.
pass_a_gloss: The rule of faith is, that we now henceforth profess what we defend, namely that one God is to be believed, and no other except the creator of the world, who has produced all things from nothing through His Word, first of all emitted; that Word, called His Son, has been seen in various ways in the name of God by the Patriarchs, always heard in the Prophets, and finally sent from the Spirit of God the Father and His power into the virgin Mary, made flesh in her womb, and born from her, has come out Jesus Christ; from there He has preached a new law and a new promise of the kingdom of heaven; has done virtues; fixed to the cross, has risen on the third day; snatched up into the heavens, has sat at the right hand of the Father; has sent the vicarious power of the Holy Spirit, who acts on believers, is to come with clarity, to take up the saints into the fruit of eternal life and the heavenly promises, and to judge the profane to perpetual fire, with the resurrection of both parts having been made with the restoration of the flesh.

choices.why: indicating the agency of the Word
specifying the context of the appearances

choices.english: vicarious power of the Holy Spirit

pass_b_english: The rule of faith is straightforward: from here on out we profess what we defend. We believe in one God, and no other—only the Creator of the world. He produced everything from nothing through His Word, which He sent forth first of all. That Word, called His Son, was seen in various ways in God's name by the Patriarchs, was always heard in the Prophets, and was finally sent from the Spirit of God the Father and His power into the virgin Mary. He was made flesh in her womb, born from her, and came forth as Jesus Christ. From there He preached a new law and a new promise of the kingdom of heaven; He performed mighty works; He was fixed to the cross and rose on the third day; He was snatched up into the heavens and sat at the right hand of the Father. He sent the vicarious power of the Holy Spirit, who acts on believers. He is to come with clarity to take up the saints into the fruit of eternal life and the heavenly promises, and to judge the profane to perpetual fire, with the resurrection of both parties accomplished and the flesh restored.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex structure of the Latin sentence, preserving the sequence of the Word's manifestations and the subsequent actions of Christ. Pass B correctly interprets 'virtutes fecisse' as 'performed mighty works' (or 'done virtues') and 'facta utriusque partis resuscitatione cum carnis restitutione' as the resurrection of both parts/parties with the restoration of the flesh.
